chapter: Duke, Gensel and the later years
title: The difficulty of keeping a big band alive
summary: Few bands paid; Thad and Mel, and Clark Terry had part-time bands.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Anyway, you had this thing going with Gensel and you
were playing some Monday nights, but what...
Yeah, but then some Monday nights at the Half Note, the old Half Note.
But what were you doing besides that in this period?

Well, I would be doing dates... If there were possible dates I could do here in New York, like on the boat rides and things like that, I'd play those. But I didn't do too much with that big band. I couldn't get too much going.
Well, it's hard to book a big band.

Yeah. Especially during that era; they just weren't using them. But I did pretty fair, considering that New York is mean, period. And to have a big band, boy, that's like... I mean, guys was talking, "Man, why don't you get your band?" I said, "Are you crazy? Nowadays you'd like for me to get a big band." What will I pay them? What will I pay them with? That's another thing.
But at that time, there were only a few bands around. Thad and Mel had the band, and then Clark had a band.
But those were all part-time things, too.
Yeah, i worked up at this place where Clark
gave me the gig. He had a gig up at the Ebony Club... Was it the Ebony Club...? Oh, I can't think of the name of that joint. I really can't think of the name...
